subject: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintechco.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@fintechco.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-05T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist — FintechCo

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for your time this morning — great discussion. Per request, here’s a concise recap of the performance SLOs we validated in the demo and the immediate MAP (Mutual Action Plan) items we recommend to qualify Redwood for your upcoming pilot.

Quick recap of what we tested today:
- Model variant: redwood-v2-medium (quantized)
- Test harness: 95th-percentile latency measurements with 120 QPS sustained traffic (burst to 200 QPS for 30s)
- Streaming: chunked-response streaming enabled, client-side SSE validated with incremental tokens
- KV cache: prefix caching validated for repeated session flows

SLOs discussed (please confirm these align with your internal goals):
- Latency: p95 <= 200ms for text-generation requests at 1-2k token context (typical flows); p99 < 350ms
- Throughput: sustained 120 QPS with <5% error rate; burst capacity to 200 QPS for up to 60s
- Concurrency: support 600 concurrent user sessions with average 3 RPS per session
- Streaming: sub-100ms first-byte for streaming start when enabled; token drift <1%

Attachments: I’ve attached the SLO checklist and the benchmark summary from today. Also attaching the anonymized workload sample you shared so we can run a focused POC benchmark.

Immediate next steps (MAP):
1) FintechCo to share production workload sample (JSON) + top 10 prompt templates — by 2028-04-07
2) Redwood to run full POC benchmark (10k synthetic users + your sample) and share a performance report — target 2028-04-12
3) Align on SLA terms and committed throughput for POC (internal procurement/legal) — FintechCo by 2028-04-15
4) Provision a reserved POC queue (Dedicated capacity) and enable streaming path + KV cache — Redwood to provision by 2028-04-13

Please let me know if you want any adjustments to the SLOs above. If these look right, we’ll proceed with the workload run once we receive the sample.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (555) 867-9021

Attachments: slo-checklist.xlsx, redwood-benchmark-summary.pdf

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@fintechco.com>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@fintechco.com>
Date: 2028-04-05T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist — FintechCo

Thanks Marissa — this is very helpful. A few quick confirmations and clarifications from our side:

- Latency: p95 <= 200ms is our preferred target for interactive flows. For background batch scoring we can accept higher latency (p95 < 800ms).
- Throughput: 120 QPS sustained is a good starting point. We need to ensure headroom for end-of-day batch bursts — can Redwood support an on-demand scaling pattern to ~500 QPS for short windows?
- Concurrency: 600 concurrent sessions is about right for the pilot scope. We’ll share expected session distribution.
- Streaming: critical for our UI; the sub-100ms first-byte target is ideal. We’ll validate client-side integration during POC.

We’ll package the workload sample and the top prompt templates and drop them into the shared Drive link by COB 2028-04-07. On the burst capacity question — can you include a short note in the benchmark report on fallback behavior (e.g., model variant downgrade, degraded throughput) and cost delta estimates?

Also looping in Sam (infra) to coordinate the procurement timeline.

—Alex
Head of Product | FintechCo

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintechco.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@fintechco.com>
Date: 2028-04-06T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist — FintechCo

Appreciate the quick replies, Alex. Yes, we can support on-demand burst scaling to ~500 QPS for short windows via Dedicated capacity + autoscaling policies; we’ll include the fallback behaviors and cost deltas in the benchmark report. High-level fallback options we’ll evaluate and document:
- Automatic route to a lower-cost quantized variant (redwood-v2-small-quant) with measured accuracy delta
- Graceful throttling with prioritized request lanes (e.g., interactive vs batch)
- Regional fallback to standby capacity if primary region is saturated

MAP update: Redwood will start the benchmark run upon receipt of your workload sample. Expect a preliminary report (latency histograms, concurrency heatmaps, streaming-first-byte timings, and a fallback/cost appendix) by 2028-04-12.

Action items for my team: Dylan will configure the benchmark harness with your sample; Aditya will run the streaming validation and capture token-level timings.

Let me know if you want a call to walk through the POC plan before we start the run.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Priya Singh <priya.singh@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintechco.com>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam.patel@fintechco.com>
Date: 2028-04-08T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist — FintechCo

Marissa / team — we uploaded the workload sample and the top 10 prompt templates to the Drive link you shared. File names: fintechco-workload-sample.json, fintechco-top10-prompts.txt.

A few notes from our infra team:
- We can provision network peering and a private endpoint for the POC; will need the IP allowlist and TLS cert requirements from Redwood.
- For cost approvals, procurement needs the expected committed throughput and a 30-day estimate for reserved capacity. Can you include an estimated TCO for the POC (based on your recommended reserved capacity)?

Sam — can you confirm when procurement will be ready to review SLA wording?

Thanks,
Priya

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya.singh@fintechco.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintechco.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-10T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist — FintechCo

Thanks Priya — we received the files and confirmed access. Next items from Redwood’s side:

1) Benchmark run scheduled: 2028-04-09 -> 2028-04-11 (we started preliminary runs; full report delivering 2028-04-12).
2) IP allowlist & TLS: attaching an IP allowlist template and TLS cert guidance in the Drive link.
3) TCO estimate for 30 days (POC reserved capacity): we’ll include a two-option estimate in the report — (A) Reserved minimal (120 QPS sustained + 200 QPS bursts) and (B) Reserved plus burst buffer (250 QPS sustained + 500 QPS bursts).

We’ll also include a brief appendix on the behavior when we hit the burst ceiling: model downgrade latency/accuracy deltas and cost per 10k extra tokens.

Propose a quick sync on 2028-04-13 to walk through the report and align on SLA language. Please confirm availability.

Appreciate the momentum — we’ll aim to make the POC results deterministic so procurement and engineering can make the decision.

Best,
Marissa
